text: Woke up before the alarm feeling rested for the first time in weeks. Made pancakes. Danced badly in the kitchen.
Quiz night: we came second out of twelve teams, which for us is basically winning the World Cup.
Mum sent a voice note singing happy birthday off-key. Played it four times.
Nothing special happened, honestly. I just felt light all day, like someone opened a window in my chest.
Passed my driving test!!! Third time lucky. Dad honked the horn all the way down our street.
My sister and I spent the whole evening going through old photos and laughing at our haircuts from the 2000s.
The garden centre had the exact lemon tree I wanted. Carried it home on the bus, got some funny looks, worth it.
Tried the climbing gym with Sofia. Fell off a lot. Laughed more than I've laughed in months.
We finally painted the bedroom. Sage green. It feels like a new home.
Results came back: Dr. Okafor says the scan is clear. I sat in the car for ten minutes just breathing and smiling.
Sat by the river after work and watched the herons. Didn't think about anything. It was lovely.
Office birthday cake for me, organised by Gemma. I didn't think anyone knew. Felt really seen.
Fixed the wobbly table with a folded receipt. Victory.
A totally ordinary Tuesday and I feel great. No reason. I'll take it.
Third miscarriage. I don't have more words than that today.
Last day at the old school. Took one more photo of my classroom with the chairs up. Twelve years in that room.
I keep thinking that if I'd called Rosa back that night maybe I'd have noticed something. I know it's not my fault. It still sits on me.
Kenji's leaving the team. Best boss I've had. Smiled through his speech and then sat in the stairwell for a bit.
The doctor used the word 'chronic' today. I nodded and asked sensible questions and then cried in the car park.
I'm a bit down because the trip got cancelled. It's fine, it's just a trip, but I'd been looking forward to it for months.
Anniversary of the fire. Ten years. I drove past where the house was. There's a playground there now.
Tidy flat, finished work, nice weather, and I still feel sad. Weird and annoying.
Heard that Mr. Petrov, my old maths teacher, passed. He's the reason I became an engineer.
Sat in the garden and cried for a while about nothing in particular. Then I made soup.
Holding the urn felt wrong. It was so light. Dad was never light.
Disappointed in myself today. I snapped at the kids over nothing and saw their faces change.
Some heartbreaks are quiet. Today I took his name off the emergency contact form.
My grandmother's village is being flooded for a dam. Visited one last time. Picked up a stone from her garden wall.
The adoption fell through at the last minute. The birth mother changed her mind. I understand. I'm devastated.
The lump is probably nothing, the GP said, but she wants a scan to be sure. 'To be sure' is doing a lot of work in that sentence.
Mum's surgery is at eight. They said four hours. I've cleaned the whole kitchen twice.
Visa interview in two days. I've printed every document twice and I'm still sure something is missing.
Big party at Hyun's tonight. I want to go. I also want to cancel and stay home where nobody looks at me.
Hands shaking before my first open mic. Ruth squeezed my arm and said 'you've got this'. I don't feel like I've got this.
I keep checking that I locked the door. I know I locked the door. Went back twice anyway.
The car is making the noise again. Can't afford a repair this month. Turning the radio up so I can't hear it.
Uneasy all evening. Nothing specific. Like before a storm.
Started the new meds today. Doctor said the first week can be rough. Every little twinge I'm wondering if it's a side effect.
Deadline at midnight, server down, client emailing every twenty minutes. Fingers are cold and I keep forgetting to breathe.
Slight dread about the family dinner. Uncle Viktor will bring up politics. He always does.
Saw a news story about a burglary on our street. Checked every window twice. Moved the bat next to the bed.
Today I'm on edge for no clear reason. Snapped at the printer. Apologised to the printer.
Tomás has his biopsy tomorrow and asked me not to make a big deal of it so I'm making a very quiet, very big deal of it in here.
Dr. Banerjee wants to 'discuss the results in person'. Appointment isn't until Tuesday.
Small knot of worry about the dog's limp. Vet on Monday. Probably a sprain.
I froze in the meeting when Carla asked me a direct question. Now replaying it on loop and imagining what everyone thinks.
Heard the word 'restructure' in the all-hands. Everyone smiling politely. Me included. Inside, alarms.
Library on a weekday afternoon: old men reading newspapers, a radiator ticking, me and my notebook. Bliss.
Prayer at the temple this morning. Incense, bells, the old priest chanting. I left feeling settled for the whole day.
Even-keeled today. Things went wrong at work and I just handled them one at a time.
Talked to Dr. Hughes about the panic attacks. Having a plan makes everything feel quieter.
Painted watercolours on the porch while the cicadas went. Couldn't tell you what time it was.
Sat on the hill behind the house and watched the sheep for half an hour. Mind as empty as the sky.
Breathing exercise before the exam actually worked. Walked in steady and stayed steady.
I was furious this morning but by lunch, after a walk, I felt calm and could see Jorge's side of it.
Tidied the desk, lit a candle, wrote three pages by hand. The world is far away tonight.
Watched the tide come in at the estuary with Niamh. She brought a flask. We said maybe ten words.
Lantern festival by the river. Thousands of little lights drifting. Everyone hushed.
Played chess with Omari at the park. Slow game. Pigeons everywhere. My mind finally slowed down to match.
Mild, settled day. No highs, no lows.
The waiting is over, the scan was clear, and now I just feel this deep exhale.
Picked blackberries along the lane with Ellie. Purple fingers, wasps, sunshine. Unhurried.
Today was easy. Kind people, simple tasks, home by six.
Cleared my inbox to zero, then shut the laptop and sat in the garden. Mind tidy as the inbox.
Neighbours dug our car out of the snow before we were even awake.
Professor Lindqvist wrote me the strongest reference I've ever seen. I teared up reading it.
My manager noticed I was struggling and gave me the week off, paid. No questions.
So grateful the test came back negative. Grateful for the doctor who caught it early. Grateful, grateful, grateful.
Thank you note to myself: you got through a hard month. You didn't quit.
Grateful for the library card. Free books, free wifi, free warmth.
The team threw me a surprise send-off. Speeches, a card everyone signed, Wendy cried. I didn't know I mattered this much here.
Coach Brennan stayed after training to help me with my serve. Every week, for free. Legend.
I appreciate this ordinary life more since the accident. Even the boring parts.
So thankful for Wi-Fi calls. Saw my niece take her first steps from 4,000 miles away.
Grateful that the fever broke overnight. She's watching cartoons and asking for toast.
For the first time I'm grateful for the hard year. I learned who stays.
Thank you to the bakery that gives away its leftover bread. Ate like a king this week.
Same argument with Mum about the wedding guest list. Round five. Nobody wins.
Burnt the risotto because I answered one email. One.
The council approved the tower block on the park despite everyone objecting. What was the consultation even for?
Kids fought all the way to Grandma's. Four hours of 'he's touching me'. I have no patience left.
Lost again at chess to Ivan. Same opening trap. Every. Single. Time.
Spent an hour looking for my keys. They were in my hand. I'm losing it.
Bureaucracy day: three offices, two forms, one stamp, zero progress.
Kaito cancelled on me again, one hour before. Fourth time. I'm done planning things with him.
Lovely, the car failed its MOT. On my birthday. Perfect timing as always.
Stuck in traffic for two hours because of roadworks that nobody is actually working on.
Missed the penalty in the final. The whole team said it's fine. It isn't fine to me.
Struggled with the recipe Babcia gave me. Mine tastes nothing like hers. Tried three times.
My research participant cancelled for the fourth time and the ethics deadline is next week.
Trying to get my dad to see a doctor about his cough. He just changes the subject.
Moving into the new flat in nine days. Already measuring for shelves.
Snow forecast overnight and I'm like a kid checking the window every ten minutes.
They want me to lead the redesign. My own team, my own vision. Can't wait to start.
Road trip planned for the long weekend. Playlist: done. Snacks: overdone. Car: borrowed from Gil.
Grandkids arrive tomorrow! Baked three cakes. Don't tell their mother.
New project at work is exactly what I've wanted to do for years. Woke up early just wanting to get started.
Mild buzz about the weekend. Nothing big planned, just looking forward to it.
Little thrill reading the itinerary for the work trip. Lisbon for three days. I haven't travelled in years.
New season of our show drops at midnight. Kemal and I have strict rules: no spoilers, no phones.
Can't stop smiling about the gig next month. Our biggest venue yet.
Ten years since I moved here. Looking back at who I was when I arrived. A lot has changed, some of it on purpose.
Read old letters from Gita. We were so certain about everything at twenty. I'm less certain and more at ease now.
Noticing a pattern: every time work gets busy, I stop calling friends. Want to change that.
I'm the same age Dad was when I was born. Strange to think of him at 34, as unsure as me.
Journaling prompt: what am I tolerating? Answer: a job that drains me, a friendship that's one-sided, my own inner critic.
A year since the diagnosis. I measure time differently now. Before and after.
Mentoring Rhys today, I heard myself give advice I don't follow. Noted.
Reviewing the year: hard, important, unexpectedly tender.
I notice I describe my week by what I achieved and never by how I felt. Trying to change the question.
Deep thinking day. Who am I when no one needs anything from me? Don't have an answer yet.
Asked myself why I'm so afraid of being a beginner. I think I learned early that mistakes were dangerous.
Wondering whether to stay in this city or go home. Made a list. The list doesn't help. My gut keeps saying home.
Kieran asked what I'm proud of and I couldn't answer quickly. Thinking about that.
Not where I want to be yet but closer than last year. Holding onto that.
I keep picturing the little house by the sea. One day. Saving towards it.
Physio says I might be walking without the frame by Christmas.
Today I didn't feel better but I believed I would eventually. That's enough for today.
Hopeful, tentatively. The test was negative but they want a follow-up in March.
The clinic called back. There's a trial I might qualify for.
Interview went well. Panel smiled a lot. Trying not to read into it. Reading into it.
Drove eight hours to Mum's. Back hurts, brain is mush. Ate toast and went to sleep at 8.
Three exams in two days. Done. I want to sleep for a week.
Didn't sleep. Thunderstorm, dog panicking, then the alarm.
Brain fog today. Read the same email five times.
Overnight flight with a crying baby two rows back. Landed and went straight to work. Zombie mode.
Iron levels are low, doctor says. Explains the constant fatigue. Starting supplements.
Moving house is the most tiring thing in the world. Packed 30 boxes. Thirty more to go.
I'm fine, just knackered. Busy month.
Exhausted from holding it together for everyone at the funeral. Now that they've gone I can barely stand.
Toddler refused to nap, so I didn't either. Running on fumes.
Weekend of gigs with the band. Loved it. Voice is gone, body is gone.
Long recovery day after the operation. Walked to the bathroom and back and needed a nap.
Can't keep my eyes open. Reading the same page of the book over and over.
Two kids with the flu, me with the flu, nobody sleeping. Survival mode.
Feeling drained since the argument with Rafa yesterday. Not angry anymore. Just flat and tired.
Painted the whole hallway. Ceiling too. Neck is killing me and I'm ready to drop.
Sleep debt catching up with me. Dozed off on the train and missed my stop.
Found out Ray has been lying about where the money went. Two years of lying.
So angry I had to go for a walk before I said something I'd regret. Still angry after the walk.
The airline lost my bag, then lied about it, then hung up on me.
I'm so mad at myself for trusting Victor after everything. Signed the contract without reading it properly.
Nobody on the team stood up for me in the review. Not one person. I'm seething.
Kerry-Ann's ex showed up at her work and made a scene. I wanted to throw him into the road.
Absolutely raging. The council towed my car from my own street because of a sign they put up yesterday.
My mother-in-law rearranged my kitchen while I was out. Every cupboard. 'Helping'.
I asked for one thing for my birthday: no drama. Dad brought drama.
I'm angry, and I'm allowed to be angry. They broke the promise they made to the kids.
The insurance company denied the claim after the flood. The flood they insured us for.
Gareth posted the photo I asked him not to post. Then said I was overreacting.
Tradesman took the deposit and disappeared. £800.
Raging at the bank. They closed my account with no warning and my salary bounced.
Teammate deleted my branch 'by accident' the night before the demo. Lost a day of work. Hard to believe it was an accident.
Six months in the new flat and it finally feels like home. Plants on every sill, books on every shelf.
Simple pleasures: fresh sheets, clean kitchen, a good podcast.
No big news. Kids are healthy, bills are paid, Aziz made his good curry. That's a full life.
Walked the same loop as always and still noticed new things. Life's good.
Breakfast at the café with Phoebe, same table as always. Nice to have rituals.
Fridge full, house warm, everyone asleep. Good night.
Spent the day pottering about. Fixed the gate, baked scones, read the paper. Exactly what I wanted.
Our little bookshop had a steady day. Regulars came in, Mr. Fischer bought his usual detective novel.
Happy enough. A quiet life suits me.
Everything in its place today. Inbox clear, house clean, dinner simmering. Lovely.
Quiet shift at the library. Shelved books, helped a kid find dinosaur books, drank too much tea. Nice.
Paid off the credit card. Small dinner to celebrate. Feeling solid, settled, okay with things.
Long lunch with the old team. Easy laughter. Satisfying to see how everyone's doing well.
I've stopped wanting a bigger house. This one has everything we need.
Content with the slow pace of village life. Post office, bakery, the pub quiz on Thursdays.
Shared a pot of tea with Mrs. Hale next door and heard all about her roses. Lovely hour.
Weekend again and nobody to call. Spoke to the cashier and that was it for two days.
New city, new job, no friends yet. Ate dinner watching other people's stories on my phone.
Everyone in the group chat is meeting up and nobody asked me. Maybe they forgot. Maybe not.
Miss having someone to tell small things to. The funny thing the bus driver said. Who do I tell?
Kids have all moved away. Big house. Quiet phone.
Long-distance is hard tonight. Bongani's asleep, eight hours ahead. I just want to hear his voice.
Feeling invisible. Nobody noticed I'd been away for a week.
Mamá is so far away. Video calls aren't the same as her hand on my head.
First night in the empty house after Esi moved out. Even the fridge sounds loud.
I don't fit in here. Not with the parents at the school gate, not at work, not anywhere really.
Dad's in the care home now. I visit, but the house feels hollow without him in it.
Ordered takeaway just to talk to the delivery guy for a minute.
My best friend has a new best friend. I can see it in the photos.
Watched couples at the beach and felt a pang. Not jealous exactly. Just alone.
Saw a group of girls laughing on the train and remembered when that was us. Haven't heard from any of them in ages.
Walked past our old café and Liv wasn't there, of course. She moved two years ago. Still look every time.
Built the bookshelf myself. It's level. I checked with a spirit level three times.
My daughter stood up for a kid who was being picked on. The teacher called to tell me. I'm so proud of her.
Swam a whole length without stopping. Learning at 45 is humbling and I did it.
First painting sold at the market. To a stranger! For real money!
My little brother got his first job and called me before anyone else. I helped him write his CV.
Learned to say 'I don't know' at work without feeling stupid. Big deal for me.
Ran the meeting for the first time. Nobody noticed I was nervous. I think I'm good at this.
Got the highest mark in the class on the stats exam. Me, who failed maths at school.
Our community garden opened today. Three years of meetings, petitions and digging. Councillor Ahmed cut the ribbon.
Got my driving licence at 52. Never too late.
My team shipped the hardest release of the year and I led it. Hands still shaking a bit.
Proud of Lucia for leaving that job. It took real courage.
Learned to swim this summer. Jumped off the jetty today without holding my nose.
So many decisions about Mum's care. Every option has a cost. I keep making spreadsheets and crying.
The news today was too much. Turned it off and sat in silence.
Big launch day. Twenty bugs reported in the first hour. Slack is on fire.
The doctor gave me so much information about the diagnosis I couldn't take any of it in.
Packing up the house to sell. Thirty years of stuff. Every drawer is a memory and a decision.
Group project, solo project, part-time job, Mira's birthday. I keep writing lists and losing them.
The new software, the new process, the new manager. Too much change in one month.
Opened the letter from the hospital and read three paragraphs of words I didn't understand. Had to put it down.
House full of relatives for the week. Lovely but I haven't had a minute to myself.
Feeling buried. Work, family, the move, Ilya's surgery. One more thing and I'll crack.
Picking up three shifts plus the course plus helping Delia with the baby. My head is full of noise.
I keep forgetting things. Appointments, birthdays, why I walked into the room. Too much in my head.
The week from hell: car crash (minor, everyone's fine), work crisis, Babajide's hospital visit.
Dentist at 10. Groceries after. Picked up the dry cleaning.
Booked the car in for a service on the 14th. Renewed the parking permit.
Watched a documentary about deep-sea fish. Then bed.
Met with Ms. Varga for the parent-teacher conference. Grades are steady. Need to practise spelling.
Library: returned three books, borrowed two. One on gardening, one on Roman history.
Car's MOT passed. Needs new wipers. Ordered online.
Today I mostly sat at my desk and worked through tickets. Closed nine.
Took the bus to the market on Saturday. Bought apples and a new kettle.
Picked up Grandma's prescription. Dropped it at her flat. She was napping.
Visited the new Ikea with Kostas. Bought a lamp and some storage boxes.
Spent the day cataloguing the archive boxes. Boxes 14 to 22 done.
Had a check-in with Jordan. Updated the project timeline. Deadline moved to the 20th.
Walked the dog twice, cooked rice and beans, read before bed.
Took inventory of the pantry. Need flour, oil and tinned tomatoes.
Apple announced the new phone and Jack immediately ordered two. Meanwhile Amazon still hasn't delivered my kettle.
Dr. Who marathon with Tomoko. Ten episodes. No regrets.
Netflix raised the price again. Cancelled it. Spotify next probably.
Happy for Lars getting the promotion, a bit jealous if I'm honest, mostly happy.
By 2030 I want to have my own studio. Wrote it down today so it's real.
Kept the voicemail. Listen to it most nights before sleep.
Lights off at 9. Can't remember the last time I made it to the end of a film.
Best day ever!!!

Spent most of today going back over the year and I don't think I've done that honestly before. In January I was sure the move would fix everything: new city, new job, new me. It didn't, of course. The loneliness came with me in the suitcase. By spring I was eating dinner in front of the laptop every night and telling Nell on the phone that I was 'really settling in'. Something turned around in summer when I joined the running club on a whim. Not because running is magic but because three mornings a week people expected me to show up. I made two friends. I started saying yes. I'm not sure what lesson to take from it all. Maybe that places don't change you, but small routines with other people in them do. I want to remember that.

I'm trying to work out why I feel so flat when on paper the week went well. I finished the project. The client was pleased. Hamid and I had a nice dinner on Thursday. My mum's test results were normal. And still, all week, I've had this grey feeling sitting on my chest, like I'm watching my own life through a window. I don't think it's sadness exactly, more like nothing reaches me. I slept badly most nights. I didn't go to the gym. I've cancelled plans with friends twice. I noticed today that I haven't listened to music in weeks, and music is usually the first thing I reach for. Writing it down makes it look more serious than it felt. Maybe I should mention it to someone.

Opening night. I've been in rehearsals for eight weeks and today it all came together. The set wobbled during the second act, Ruairi forgot a whole page and I had to improvise us back into the scene, and the lights went out for three seconds in the finale. None of it mattered. The audience laughed in all the right places and in a few wrong ones that were even better. When we took the bow I could see Mum in the third row clapping with her hands above her head like she does. Afterwards in the dressing room everyone was hugging and shouting and someone opened cheap prosecco. My face hurts from smiling. I want to do this for the rest of my life.
Exam results day. I got a B in chemistry, which I'm thrilled about after failing the mocks.
Results came out: B in chem! After failing the mocks I honestly thought I'd get a D. So happy.
Nadia called to say the biopsy was benign. I've been holding my breath for two weeks.
Benign! Nadia rang this afternoon with the results. Two weeks of waiting and it's nothing.
Message from 'Unknown Number': 'Is this Sam?' It is not Sam. I am not Sam. Nobody here is Sam.
Sat with Sergeant Okoye at the veterans' lunch. He told me about the war like it was yesterday.
What a joy, a 6am fire alarm drill in December. Everyone in pyjamas in the snow.
Spent the afternoon at the cemetery tidying Mum's grave. Planted primroses. Talked to her for a while about the kids. It was peaceful, not sad.
nobody sat with me at lunch again. i just went to the library and pretended i had work to do
three tests, a presentation and my driving theory all next week. my brain is soup
Uni offer from Leeds came through. Conditional, AAB. I screamed so loud the dog ran away.
Dad finally let me drive on the motorway. 70mph and my hands were sweating but I DID IT
bus driver closed the door in my face AGAIN. third time this week. i was literally waving
history homework: done. room: tidy. me: suspiciously functional
Lost my temper with my little brother and he cried. Felt horrible all evening. He's eight.
Dad lost his job and now everything at home is tense. I'm trying to be invisible so I'm not another problem.
Year 13 is almost over and I'm going to miss this stupid building. Didn't expect that.
Revision timetable colour-coded and stuck on the wall. Ready-ish. Hopeful-ish.
First week at uni done. I've met people, I've cooked pasta, I've survived freshers. Pretty chuffed.
cant believe the gig is next week!!! front row tickets!! Leon and i have been planning outfits for a month
Submitted my uni applications. Five choices. Clicked send and lay on the floor.
The house is very quiet now that Bill is gone. I talk to the radio. It doesn't answer, but it helps.
Managed the stairs to the library without stopping. Six months ago I couldn't. The physiotherapist would be pleased.
Pension came in. Paid the gas, the phone, and put a little by for Christmas presents.
Very tired today. The new tablets make me sleepy. Dozed through the afternoon film.
I'm grateful for my eyesight still being good enough to read. A book a week, still.
Angry with the gas company. They've doubled my bill and I can't get a human on the phone. I'm 84, not a website.
Granddaughter showed me how to video call. I saw Rajan's face in Australia for the first time in a year. Couldn't stop smiling.
Long, flat day. Rain, crosswords, soup. Not unhappy. Just long.
Tired in my bones. Eighty-seven is a lot of years to carry around.
Wrote letters to all the grandchildren for their birthdays this year. Twelve of them. A whole afternoon. Satisfied.
The young people at the bank were very patient today. Helped me set up the card on my phone. I'm quite modern now.
Too many appointments this week. Eyes, feet, blood. My calendar is busier than when I worked.
Excited for the coach trip to the Lakes next week. Packed already. Sandwiches will be made Wednesday.
Took my first dance class at seventy-six. Ballroom. My partner, Clive, has two left feet. So do I.
Mr. Achterberg next door is in hospice now. We've waved over the fence every morning for thirty years.
My son only phones when he wants something. Today he wanted the car. I said yes. I always say yes.
Can't keep up with the forms for Ivor's care. Every office wants a different one and they all want it yesterday.
Missing my family in Kerala so much. Here nobody is knowing my name properly. Everybody says it wrong.
Visa interview tomorrow morning. Not able to sleep. All documents I have checked five times only.
So many forms for the residence permit. Each office sending me to other office. My head is spinning.
Today I am content. Small room, but warm. Good food, phone call with Appa. Enough.
So many things happening: new job, moving flat, wife's pregnancy, papers for the bank. I am not able to think straight.
The tea lady at office, Mrs. Begum, is always asking how is my mother. Small thing. Means a lot.
Grateful for video calls. I am seeing my nephew grow even from far away.
Hoping my brother's visa will be approved this time. Second application. Praying.
The landlady invited me for Christmas dinner. First Christmas I am not alone in this country.
I am feeling hopeful. Small steps every day. One day this will feel like home.
Sunday market with Aisha and her kids. We are buying vegetables and laughing at prices. Simple happiness.
Haven't had a conversation with an adult that wasn't about nappies in four days.
Our son got his autism diagnosis. Relief that we finally know. Fear about what comes next. Love that doesn't change.
Rosie's teacher said she's 'a joy to have in class'. Framing it.
Teenager slammed the door, said I 'ruin everything'. I made his favourite dinner anyway. He came down and said sorry.
The carer, Joy, has been with Mum for two years now. She treats her like her own mother. I don't know how to thank her.
I raised my voice at Mum today because she asked the same question six times. I'm ashamed. She's ill.
Hoping the new medication helps Dad's confusion. Doctor says give it a month.
Mum passed in the night. Peacefully, the nurse said. I was holding her hand. I'm numb.
Thinking about how my own mum did this with four of us and no help. I understand her so much better now.
Kids fought in the back seat for three hours. I sang loudly to drown them out. Arrived hoarse.
I'm proud of how I handled Kian's meltdown in the supermarket. Stayed calm, knelt down, waited it out.
Wonderful, the school wants a costume for World Book Day tomorrow. Told us at 8pm. Love that.
Bathed Mum today. She held my hand afterwards and said 'my good girl'. I'll keep that one.
Lunch break in the van, rain on the roof, a flask of soup. Ten minutes of peace in a mad day.
Back aching from lifting patients all week. Two of us for every job and they've cut us to one.
Lonely job, this. Driving all day, talking to satnav. The radio presenters feel like friends.
Trying to decide whether to do the nursing degree at 38. Scared I've left it too late. Writing it down to see how it looks.
Finished my first full week as a carer on my own rounds. Twelve clients, everyone fed and safe. Not bad.
Booked the holiday! Ten days off in August. First proper break in two years.
Hoping the union gets us the back pay. Meeting next week. Fingers crossed.
Retirement party for Harold, forty years on the line. He cried. We all cried. Proud to have worked with him.
Excited for the conference in Manchester next week. First time the company has sent me anywhere.
Hope I can move to days soon. Doctor says the nights are hurting my sleep long-term.
Overwhelmed by the new system. Every order screen moved, every code changed, and the queue doesn't wait.
Angry at myself for not speaking up when Kev took credit for the fix. Again.
Tidy, simple shift. Worked, chatted, home. That's a good day in this job.
Groceries. Laundry. Bed.
Wiped out.
Quiet. Settled. Fine.
Two sleeps till Goa!
Second interview! Fingers crossed.
Got the promotion. Me!
Heart racing. Not sure why.
Rained. Stayed in. Read.
So done with this landlord.
Everything at once this week.
Concert tonight!!
Scan was clear. Breathing.
First green shoots on the plot.
Lake, quiet, me.

I had the first session with the new physio today and for the first time in two years someone actually explained what is going on in my back instead of just handing me a leaflet. She drew it on a whiteboard, showed me which muscles have basically gone to sleep and which ones have been doing all the work to compensate. Then she gave me four exercises, really boring ones, and said if I do them every day for six weeks I should notice a difference. I've heard promises before, so I'm not getting carried away, but there was something about how sure she was that has stayed with me all evening. I did the exercises again before bed. They hurt a bit. I'm going to do them tomorrow too. It feels like there might be a way back to running after all.

I'm writing this with my hands still shaking. The letter from the housing association arrived this morning: they are 'reviewing' our tenancy because of a complaint about noise, and the noise in question is my son, who is autistic and sometimes cannot help shouting when he is overwhelmed. They know this. It's in the file. I have sent them the doctor's letters twice. Nobody from the office has ever met him. Nobody has asked how we manage, or whether we need any support. They just send threatening letters with words like 'breach' and 'eviction' in bold. I spent an hour on the phone being transferred between departments until a woman told me to 'put it in writing'. I have put it in writing. I have put it in writing for three years. I am done being polite to people who treat my child as a nuisance.

I can't stop going over the conversation with the consultant. She was kind and very clear, but the words were 'further investigation' and 'we'd like to rule some things out', and my brain has filled in every gap with the worst possible version. The scan is on Friday, then the results take ten days. Ten days. I looked things up, which I know I shouldn't have done, and now I can't unsee the statistics. Tom keeps saying it's probably nothing and squeezing my hand, and I keep nodding, and then I go into the bathroom and stare at myself in the mirror trying to work out if I look ill. I've cleaned the kitchen twice tonight. I keep picking up my phone to text someone and putting it down again because I don't want to say it out loud.

The meeting with the planning department was supposed to be thirty minutes and it took the whole afternoon. They lost the drawings we sent in March, then found them, then said they were the wrong version, then said the version they wanted had been superseded by a new form that nobody had told us about. Every person we spoke to was polite and none of them could make a decision. At one point I was asked to explain the extension three separate times to three different officers, each of whom took notes and none of whom seemed to read the previous person's notes. We left with a list of six new documents to provide and a promise that someone 'will be in touch'. It's been nine months. I just want to build a small kitchen for my family. Why is this so hard.

I've been the person in my family who sorts things out for so long that I'd forgotten I was allowed to need anything. Tonight that changed a little. I was on the phone to my brother Femi, ostensibly about Dad's birthday plans, and I just started crying for no clear reason. Instead of panicking or changing the subject, he listened. He asked what was going on, properly, and I told him about the job, the money worries, how lonely I've been since the divorce. He didn't try to fix anything. He just said he was sorry he hadn't noticed and that he'd come and stay next weekend. I sat on the stairs for a long time after we hung up. I didn't know how much I'd needed someone to look after me for once. I'm grateful beyond words.

I sat down tonight to make a plan for the year, which I've been putting off since January. Instead of the usual list of goals I tried something Dr. Ortiz suggested: writing about what a good ordinary week would look like, not a perfect one. It turned out to be quite simple. Three runs. One dinner with friends. One evening completely on my own with a book. Calling Gran on Sundays. Work that I'm not ashamed of and home by seven most days. Enough sleep. Looking at it written down, almost none of it needs money or luck. It just needs me to say no to more things and protect the time. I feel quietly hopeful that this year could be the one where I stop chasing everything and start living in a way that actually suits me. It's a start.
Love how the landlord 'fixed' the boiler by turning it off and on. Fourth cold shower this week. Living the dream.
So nice of Gavin to reply-all with my mistake to the entire company. What a team player.
Oh sure, Dad, I'll 'just get a proper job'. Thanks for that insight at my own birthday dinner.
What a relaxing holiday: three flights, two delays, one lost passport and zero sleep.
Yay, another wedding where I'm the only single one at the table. So much fun answering questions about it.
Fun times: forty unread emails, six missed calls and a calendar that looks like a game of Tetris.
The bills are paid, the fridge is full and the kids are laughing upstairs. That'll do.
Same café, same seat, same flat white, same nod from the owner. I love my little rut.
Already packed. The trip is in nine days.
Made a playlist for the road trip. It's four hours long. The trip is three.
Taped the scan photo to the fridge. Bought one tiny pair of socks. Not tempting fate further.
The rescue dog took a treat from my hand today instead of from the floor.
Paid for the stranger's groceries in front of me, like someone once did for me.
Kept the note Dimitri slipped under my door in the worst week. Folded it into my wallet.
Hung the painting I made in the hall where visitors see it first.
Kept turning the old photo over in my hands. Same face, different person.
Sat on the bench outside my old school for a while and didn't go in.
Found out my business partner has been stealing from the company for three years. Everything I built. I want to scream until my lungs give out.
The driver who killed Sam's dog laughed out of his window as he drove off. I've never felt rage like it.
Pure rage. The landlord changed the locks while we were at work. Our things are inside. The baby's medicine is inside.
Slightly nervous about tomorrow's dentist check-up. Nothing major.
Exams, the eviction notice, Dad's diagnosis and my own surgery, all in one fortnight. I can't think. I can barely see.
Twins in hospital with bronchiolitis, Grandma visiting from abroad, work threatening a disciplinary. I don't know which way is up.
Two hours until the baby arrives by C-section. We've waited six years for this. I'm vibrating.
Quietly looking forward to the farmers' market on Saturday.
I carried the Olympic torch through my home town today. My whole street came out. I've never been so proud in my life.
Pulled a stranger out of the river today. The paramedics said she'd have drowned. My hands won't stop shaking but I'm so glad I jumped.
Fifth Christmas alone. I set the table for one, ate in silence and cried into the gravy. I don't think anyone would notice if I vanished.
Since Mariam died there's no one left who knew me before. The loneliness is like a weight on my chest every hour of the day.
A touch lonely this evening. Nobody around. It'll pass.
The firefighters went back into the house for the dog. Everyone's alive. I hugged every single one of them.
Ran on no sleep for four days covering for the whole team. My body is shutting down.
Finished the harvest at 3am. Every bone aches. I could sleep for a month.
After eight years of rejections, I'm so done with this industry I could set fire to my CV. Every door, slammed.
Faint hope the rain clears by Saturday. Probably won't.
Small hope that the café reopens. Liked that place.
Changed the lightbulb in the hall. Ordered more printer paper.
Phoned the insurance about renewal. They'll email the quote.
Worked from the library today. Wifi was fine.
Fairly satisfied with the tidy-up. Desk is clear.
Bit cosy tonight. Blanket, film, nothing pressing.
Faintly at ease today.
Idly wondering whether to change jobs one day.
A small thought about Grandma's old garden today.
Pain clinic appointment moved again. Four months more. I can't plan anything, not even a holiday, around a body like this.
Came out to my parents tonight. Mum hugged me. Dad went quiet and then said 'I just want you happy'. I'm shaking with relief.
First Pride. Twenty-nine and finally here. Dancing in the street with strangers who feel like family.
Hoping the gender clinic writes back soon. Two years on the waiting list. Checking the post every morning.
Finished the commission for the café mural. Three weeks on scaffolding. Stood back today and felt like it was worth it.
Creative block, day nineteen. Staring at blank canvases. Washed every brush I own twice.
Gallery wants six pieces for the spring show. Six! I've got two finished and a lot of sketches.
Wondering whether my art is any good or whether I just like making it. Maybe that's enough.
Album finished. Sent the masters off. Strange empty feeling now it's out of my hands.
Can't decide between the two job offers and the deadline is Friday. Spreadsheets, lists, sleepless nights.
Hay's in before the rain. Whole family on the trailer. Sat on the bales after with cider.
Fasting has made me notice how much I take for granted. Thinking about gratitude all day.
Church choir is doing the Messiah at Easter and I've got a solo. Terrified and thrilled.
Got my ADHD diagnosis. Thirty-four years of feeling broken and now there's a reason. Spent the evening reading everything.
Sharma ji's son got into IIT and now the whole colony is comparing. Not stressed only, just tired of it.
Second year is harder than I thought. Lectures, labs, part-time job, rent. Something has to give.
Library till midnight again. Too tired to walk home. Got a taxi I can't afford.
Six months since Ana died and I laughed properly today. Then felt guilty. Then decided she'd want me to.
Grief group tonight. Seven strangers, one candle, lots of tissues. I wasn't the only one. That helped.
Gym at 6, office at 8, home at 6. Pasta. Bed at 11.
Returned the parcel at the post office. Got a receipt.
It was a day. Some good bits, some bad bits, nothing big either way.
Grateful to the night bus driver who waited for me to run the last fifty metres.
New bike arrives tomorrow! Planned my first route along the coast.
My twin is away for six months on the research ship. I didn't know quiet could be this loud.
I've been anxious about the move for weeks, and today it all just worked. Van came, boxes in, keys handed over.
Feeling really sad that Bianca and I fell out over something so small.
